name: Associa

paper.title: Bridging Intuitive Associations and Deliberate Recall: Empowering LLM Personal Assistant with Graph-Structured Long-term Memory

construction.unit: event-centric graph: utterance, event, event-time, entity and user nodes with six edge types
construction.kept_as: verbatim user utterances linked to LLM-extracted events, inferred times and (subject, relation, object) triplets
construction.processing: one LLM prompt per dialogue unit extracts events with an absolute time, a description and triplets; every node is linked to its source utterance

organization.structure: one graph per user history; events, entities and times hang off the utterances they came from
organization.stores: memory graph plus the utterance store it points to
organization.index: Contriever embeddings of nodes and edges; FAISS for duplicate detection

management.operations: merge near-duplicate events, entities and relations: FAISS similarity merge as memories arrive, plus agglomerative clustering in batches

retrieval.query: question; a fine-tuned 3B model names missing entities, each appended to the question for another search (max_iter 2)
retrieval.candidates: cosine prizes on nodes and edges, top-15 each with rank-decayed prizes; Prize-Collecting Steiner Tree gives a connected subgraph (edge cost 0.5)
retrieval.selection: personalized PageRank over the merged subgraph, seeded by prizes, ranks the utterances
retrieval.budget: top 5 / top 10 utterances in the retrieval evaluation; QA context size not stated

use.context: retrieved user utterances (how many is not stated)

classify.note: Dense prizes seed a Steiner-tree subgraph and PageRank ranks utterances by a fixed top-k; the fine-tuned model only decides whether to search again, with which extra entities.

stages.ingestion: Only user-side turns are used; on LoCoMo two dialogue turns (four utterances) form one unit because single utterances carry little information.
stages.construction: An LLM (Qwen-Turbo) reads each timestamped unit and returns events with an inferred absolute time, a description and (subject, relation, object) triplets; entities cover objects, people, places, goals, interests, sentiments and more.
stages.organization: Events, times, entities, the user and the source utterances form one graph with six edge types (event-time, event-fact-utterance, event-entity, utterance-entity, user-asks-utterance, entity-relation-entity).
stages.update: Duplicate events, entities and relations are merged: incrementally with FAISS above a similarity threshold, and in batches with agglomerative clustering. Nothing is deleted.
stages.retrieval: Nodes and edges get cosine prizes against the question (top-15 each, decaying by rank); a Prize-Collecting Steiner Tree extracts a connected subgraph. A fine-tuned Qwen2.5-3B reads the subgraph and names missing entities; each is appended to the question and searched again (max_iter 2). Personalized PageRank then ranks the nodes.
stages.answer: GPT-4o answers from the retrieved utterances; the paper gives no QA prompt or context size.
stages.learning: The deliberating model is Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct fine-tuned on CoQA-derived samples labeled with qwen-plus: output {} when the subgraph holds the gold cue, otherwise the missing entities.

summary: Event-centric graph memory over a user's dialogue history, read by prize-collecting Steiner-tree subgraph search, a small fine-tuned model that asks for missing entities, and PageRank ranking of utterances.
notes: Venue: Findings of ACL 2025, pages 17533-17547, verified on the ACL Anthology page and the PDF footer. No arXiv version found. CODE: the paper gives no code link and a GitHub search found no official repository, so the record follows the paper only. The in-text citation for MemoRAG points to Izacard et al. 2021 (Contriever), an error in the paper.

sources.code_note: No official code: the paper has no repository link, and a GitHub search for the method name and title found none. Everything below follows the paper; unstated settings (similarity thresholds, PageRank damping, QA context size) are left null.

headline: Utterances are kept verbatim; the LLM-extracted events, times and triplets act as a graph index pointing back to them.
Retrieval is a Steiner-tree subgraph over dense prizes, widened once by a fine-tuned 3B model that lists missing entities, then ranked by PageRank.
The gains are large on LongMemEval-S retrieval (R@5 0.87 vs 0.75 for BGE) but small on LoCoMo (0.74 vs 0.71) and on QA (0.81 vs 0.80).

units.name: Utterance node
units.role: the original user turn (LoCoMo: two turns)

fields.name: text
fields.what: the user's words with their timestamp

units.name: Event node
units.role: a user-related event, the hub of the graph

fields.name: event + description
fields.what: short event name and a description

fields.name: event time
fields.what: absolute time inferred from the utterance timestamp; stored as its own node

units.name: Entity and relation
units.role: objects, people, places, goals, interests, sentiments in the event
units.made_by: LLM extraction as (subject, relation, object) triplets

fields.name: triplets
fields.what: entity nodes joined by relation edges; also linked to their event and utterance

units.name: User node
units.role: the speaker, linked to every utterance they asked

write.how: one prompt per timestamped unit returns events, inferred absolute times, descriptions and triplets, or [] if nothing about the user
write.out: 4,181 tokens per LoCoMo session, 2,303 per LongMemEval-S session

write.how: add nodes and six typed edges; every event and entity keeps an edge to its source utterance
merge events, entities and relations whose FAISS similarity exceeds a threshold as they arrive; agglomerative clustering in batches

read.how: top-k nodes and top-k edges get prize k - rank + 1, others 0
edges with prize above the cost become virtual nodes; PCST picks the connected subgraph maximizing prizes minus costs

read.input: question + subgraph shown as events, triplets and chunks
read.how: fine-tuned Qwen2.5-3B returns missing entities and unrelated content; empty means stop
a new PCST subgraph per clue, merged into the first
personalized PageRank over the merged subgraph; preference = node prize, edge weight 1 / (1 + log(1 + cost))
read.out: ranked utterances; retrieval scored at top 5 and top 10

answer_context.note: The paper gives no QA prompt, and no number of utterances passed to GPT-4o; whether events or triplets are also shown is not stated.

compression.basis: Not reported: the paper does not say how many utterances reach the answer model.

open_questions: How much of the retrieval gain comes from the graph and how much from Contriever prizes plus PageRank? w/o AM drops to Contriever level (0.67 R@5), but no run ranks utterances by prize alone.
w/o DM equals Associa max_iter=1 exactly (0.84 / 0.85 / 0.90 / 0.87), so the deliberation round adds 0.03 R@5 on LongMemEval-S.

discussion.takeaway: Index a user's dialogue history with an event-and-entity graph, pull a connected evidence subgraph instead of top-k passages, and let a small tuned model ask for what is missing. This gives clearly better evidence recall on LongMemEval and small gains on LoCoMo and QA.

claims.claim: Graph association plus deliberate recall retrieves evidence better than dense retrievers.
claims.evidence: LongMemEval-S R@5 0.87 vs 0.75 (BGE); LongMemEval-M 0.66 vs 0.56; LoCoMo 0.74 vs 0.71 (LongMemEval pipeline). Table 1
QA 0.81 / 0.66 / 0.69 vs 0.80 / 0.64 / 0.62 (LongMemEval w UF) and LightRAG 0.64 / - / 0.64. Table 2

claims.claim: Every module helps; the association mechanism most.
claims.evidence: R@5 0.67 w/o AM, 0.52 w/o EIR, 0.84 w/o DM, 0.84 w/o SFT vs 0.87. Table 3
fewest tokens per session (4,181 vs 7,085 LightRAG on LoCoMo), 0.52 s per session. Table 4, App. C.1
Qwen-7B with 2 rounds reaches R@5 0.85 on LongMemEval-S. Table 6

limits: Temporal information is not modeled in retrieval.
reading: Recall@N counts 1 only if all evidence is in the top N, so it is stricter than the per-item recall other papers report.
Associa uses only user-side turns and drops the few questions whose evidence is not in user turns (§5.2.1); the paper does not say whether the baselines were scored on the same reduced set.
Text says removing evidence ranking gives better recall@10, but Table 3 shows 0.85 vs 0.93 for the full model.
w/o DM equals Associa max_iter=1 on every metric, so 'deliberating module' and 'second round' are the same ablation.
The QA gain over the LongMemEval pipeline is 0.01 on LongMemEval-S and 0.02 on -M; only LoCoMo shows a clear margin (0.69 vs 0.62).
No code is released, and thresholds (dedup similarity, PageRank damping) and the QA context size are not given, so the system cannot be rebuilt from the paper alone.
LongMemEval (w UF and TF) is not run on LoCoMo because LoCoMo questions lack timestamps, and LightRAG is missing on LongMemEval-M.

abstract.text: Associa is a long-term memory for LLM personal assistants that indexes a user's past dialogue as an event-centric graph of events, times, entities and the original utterances. At question time it scores graph nodes and edges against the query and extracts a connected evidence subgraph with a prize-collecting Steiner tree. A small fine-tuned model then lists entities the subgraph still lacks, triggering further searches, and PageRank ranks the collected utterances. On LongMemEval and LoCoMo the authors report higher evidence recall and QA accuracy than dense retrievers and memory baselines.
